item.title: Coordinate Revisions to a Bilingual Welcome Sheet
item.prompt_text: A bilingual welcome sheet uses short phrases for directions. Several volunteers want to replace them with longer explanations because the shortest phrases can sound abrupt in one language. Printing space is fixed, and three directions matter as soon as a visitor enters. Recommend a revision approach that distinguishes immediate instructions from optional reassurance and shows how to test both languages.
item.audience: a community centre team revising a welcome sheet
item.target_grammar: Nuanced comparison, concession and explicit conditions for keeping a phrase.
item.target_structure: Name the visitor task, revise a concrete example, and use a comparable test for each language.

checklist.point: Explain why entry-stage directions need to remain easy to act on.
Give a concrete example of a short respectful alternative.
Explain where optional explanation can go.
Give a comparable check for both languages.
